newsitem.title: USA: USDA plans Web site, seminar on farmers' risk mgmt.
newsitem.headline: USDA plans Web site, seminar on farmers' risk mgmt.

text.p: Farmers puzzled by new financial instruments and programmes to protect their crops will soon have a site on the World Wide Web to help them separate the wheat from the chaff.
The Department of Agriculture said Thursday it planned to launch a Web page in the near-future to help farmers prepare for the removal of most federal controls on what farmers plant.

"There's been a profusion of new risk management tools to hit the market," said Ken Ackerman, acting administrator of the Agriculture Department's risk management agency. "This cannot be a one-size-fits-all operation."

The tools include crop insurance, revenue insurance, futures trading, so-called forward contracts, and other products that have sprung up since last year when Congress ended some 60 years of federal farm programmes. One of the major changes in the federal farm bill last year was the elimination of disaster payments for farmers.
The Web site will include educational materials, market information, fact sheets and contacts that farmers can use.
"A corn farmer in Iowa, a dairy farmer in Wisconsin and a citrus grower in Florida all have different needs," Ackerman said.
